scorecard: 71 drafts from 37 companies: facts 100% from the pack; every check passed by 0/71 (46/71 if the signature's website link is allowed)
eval:qc 7080/7080 (100.0%), 0 false positives; this suite's mutations 833/1397 (59.6%); 10 of 24 mutation types never caught
13 outside calls over 6 services; LEAKS on 2 path(s): llm:reply_classify (director name); llm:reply_classify (mobile, number written "+91 9876 543 210", number written "0522 4012345")
48 pairs: precision 100.0%, recall 47.1% (linked or sent to review 29/34); websites 27/30, directories and social networks rejected 22/23; web search egress clean

findings.title: Reply classification sends a founder's name and phone numbers to the LLM gateway
failing: reply_classify: a signature without a "-- " line: director name
reply_classify: numbers written other ways: mobile, number written "+91 9876 543 210", number written "0522 4012345"
findings.why: When the rules are unsure, the reply's new text goes to the gateway's small model (an outside service, possibly outside India, per the legal pack's processor question). newText() drops the signature only after a "-- " line, which most people never type, so "Regards, <name>, Director" goes out; scrub() removes emails and mobiles written 98765 43210, but not a mobile grouped +91 9876 543 210 nor a landline such as 0522 4012345. Leaked here: director name, mobile, number written "+91 9876 543 210", number written "0522 4012345". The design's rule is never a person's data to an outside service, and classify.js says the model sees the reply "with every address and number taken out".

findings.title: The gate does not re-check recipient.use_website_email: a website address drafted while the switch was on is still sent after it is turned off
failing: stop.website_address_switch_turned_off: send (gate: ok)
findings.why: The switch exists because the lawyer has not yet approved writing to website addresses (legal pack, question 2). If the answer is no and the switch goes off, every approved draft to a website address still in the queue is sent anyway, because the gate accepts the basis published_by_company whatever the switch says. A one-line check at the gate closes it.

findings.title: The quality check misses wrong facts whose digits appear elsewhere in the evidence pack
failing: date.us_format_wrong (a wrong date written "Month D, YYYY"): caught 20/34
date.swapped (two deadlines' dates swapped): caught 0/20
section.near_miss (a section one letter off (s.10A as s.10B)): caught 0/22
form.truncated (a form code cut short (INC-20A as INC-20)): caught 0/35
amount.figure_from_a_date (an invented amount whose figure appears in a date of the pack): caught 0/64
amount.misattributed (a scheme amount from the pack given to the wrong scheme): caught 1/2
findings.why: facts.numbers checks each number in a draft against the set of every digit string in the pack, without context, and facts.forms accepts any form that is a substring of the pack's text. So "₹13 lakh" passes when a date in the pack is the 13th, two deadlines' dates can be swapped, "INC-20A" can become "INC-20" and "s.10A" "s.10B". The templates make none of these mistakes (Eval 1: no factual error in any draft), but the AI drafter could, and once approval.mode becomes "sample" (HANDOVER, design 7.5) 80% of drafts that pass this check are sent without a person reading them.

findings.title: The gate accepts a recipient labelled "consent" without looking in the consent ledger
failing: stop.consent_label_without_consent: send
findings.why: config/outreach.json lists consent as a legal basis for email, and the gate checks only the label on the message. No drafting path creates such a recipient today (recipientFor gives only published_under_law or published_by_company), so this is defence in depth: the day a consented address is used for email, the gate should confirm the consent is in the ledger and not withdrawn, as the WhatsApp and call paths already do.

findings.title: A company whose CIN was issued outside UP is emailed if its record says state UP
failing: stop.cin_says_not_up (CIN U62099DL2026PTC300102): send
findings.why: "UP only" is enforced by the database on the state field alone. The CIN carries the state of registration (characters 7-8); a record mislabelled upstream is contacted. A cheap cross-check in the validator or the gate would hold the promise even when an ingest step is wrong.

findings.title: The quality check misses an extra link written as a bare domain, a director named, another company's name in the greeting, a penalty threat in other words, urgency in other words, a claim that a filing was not made, in other words
failing: link.extra_bare_domain (an extra link written as a bare domain): caught 0/68
person.director_named (a director named): caught 0/68
company.other_in_greeting (another company's name in the greeting): caught 0/68
tone.penalty_paraphrase (a penalty threat in other words): caught 0/68
tone.urgency_paraphrase (urgency in other words): caught 0/68
tone.missed_paraphrase (a claim that a filing was not made, in other words): caught 0/68
findings.why: The tone rules are fixed phrase lists, so "Please file on time to avoid penalties" or "this filing was not made on time" pass; links are found only after http(s):// or www.; nothing checks names. A person reading every draft catches these, which is why they rank below the factual misses; under sample approval they would reach founders.

findings.title: Long company names make the reviewed templates fail their own length limits
failing: navyarth/first_touch/en: subject 94 characters (limit 90); body 253 words (limit 250)
navyarth/follow_up/en: subject 98 characters (limit 90)
omvara/follow_up/en: subject 94 characters (limit 90)
findings.why: The first subject is "<name>: your next filing dates" and a follow-up adds "Re: ", so a name over 66 characters (62 for a follow-up) breaks the 90-character limit, and a long name repeated in a full pack pushes the body past 250 words. Such a draft is stored as qc_failed: a person must shorten it by hand before it can be approved, every time, and under sample approval it never goes by the engine's route. MCA allows names this long; the templates could shorten the subject instead (for example without "Private Limited").

findings.title: Every template email carries a third link (the sender's website in the signature)
failing: 71/71 drafts: other links: https://solutionai.in
findings.why: templates.js promises "one link to the company's page and one to unsubscribe", and the AI prompt says the page link is "the only link", yet the signature it must copy word for word holds https://solutionai.in. qc.js deliberately allows it. Harmless in itself, but the promise, the prompt and the code disagree; decide which is meant.

findings.title: follow_up emails do not say why the founder is getting them
failing: 24 drafts: aarvik/follow_up/en, bhuvira/follow_up/hi, chandral/follow_up/hi, dhanvio/follow_up/en, ekansh/follow_up/hi, falgun/follow_up/en, garvisha/follow_up/en, hemkosh/follow_up/hi and 16 more
findings.why: First and new-need emails end with where the address came from (the MCA register or the company's own website); follow-ups end with the unsubscribe link only. A founder who sees only the follow-up (the first went to spam) is never told the source, which matters most for a website address, the basis the lawyer has not yet approved.

findings.title: Transliteration variants of the same name are not even put in front of a reviewer
failing: translit.shri_shree: not linked (best candidate too weak or contradicted)
translit.laxmi_lakshmi: not linked (no company with a similar name in the CIN universe we hold)
translit.devanagari: not linked (no company with a similar name in the CIN universe we hold)
translit.compound_word: not linked (no company with a similar name in the CIN universe we hold)
translit.two_vowels: not linked (no company with a similar name in the CIN universe we hold)
findings.why: Laxmi/Lakshmi, Shri/Shree, a name typed in Devanagari: the founder's company is in the universe but no candidate reaches the review queue, so the startup stays unlinked and its facts never join the company record. Precision is unharmed; recall on Hindi-belt names is.

findings.title: Name normalisation calls two different one-letter-apart names "the same but for a slip"
failing: near.one_letter_names
findings.why: typo_of treats Hiranyo and Hiranya as one name misspelt. In this run the matcher still did not link them automatically (the probability stayed under the threshold), but the name rule alone offers no protection; it relies on the other conditions.

findings.title: Website confirmation takes a free site-builder subdomain for the company's own site
failing: builder.weebly: https://tarovikagrofoods.weebly.com/
findings.why: wixsite.com, blogspot.com and godaddysites.com are refused as shared hosts, but other builders (weebly.com here; similarly jimdo, webnode, myshopify) are not. The contact step then looks for role addresses on that subdomain, so the practical harm is small, but the rule should be a list of kinds, not a handful of names.

findings.title: Website confirmation rejects real company sites whose names are initials or whose domains drop "Shri"
failing: own.two_letter_initials: https://vnagro.example/
own.honorific_dropped: https://ganeshagro.example/
findings.why: distinctive() drops words under three letters and domain_fits() requires the first distinctive word in the domain, so "VN Agro" has no distinctive word at all and "Shri Ganesh Agro" at ganeshagro.* fails. Safe (nothing wrong is accepted) but those companies never get a website address.

findings.title: Docs and code disagree
failing: CAPS_FILE is read (services/src/config.js:32) but not in .env.example
DKIM_SELECTOR is read (services/src/ops/preflight.js:172) but not in .env.example
SARVAM_API_BASE is read (services/src/voice/sarvam.js:90) but not in .env.example
<MAILBOX_n>_SMTP_USER is read (services/src/outreach/transport.js:30) but not in .env.example
findings.why: The handover is what the team runs the engine from after 25 November; a variable missing from .env.example is a setting nobody will know to set (DKIM_SELECTOR changes what preflight checks).
